slot.brief: Show a rectangular loop entering/exiting a uniform B-field region at constant speed; give induced emf as a function of time and ask for a specific value (or the emf at a given position) using flux change over time.

stem: A rectangular loop moves to the right at $0.50\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ as shown in the figure. At $t=0.80\ \text{s}$, its clockwise induced emf is $+0.030\ \text{V}$. Find the magnitude of the magnetic field.

verdicts.working: As the loop leaves the into-page field, the flux decreases and the induced current is clockwise. The changing area rate is (0.12 m)(0.50 m s⁻¹), so B = 0.030/[0.12(0.50)] = 0.50 T.

working:
$t_{\text{exit,start}}=\dfrac{0.30}{0.50}=0.60\ \text{s}$; $t_{\text{exit,end}}=\dfrac{0.30+0.20}{0.50}=1.00\ \text{s}$; hence $t=0.80\ \text{s}$ is during exit. $\mathcal{E}=Bhv\Rightarrow B=\dfrac{0.030}{(0.12)(0.50)}=0.50\ \text{T}$.

Independent check: As the loop leaves the into-page field, the flux decreases and the induced current is clockwise. The changing area rate is (0.12 m)(0.50 m s⁻¹), so B = 0.030/[0.12(0.50)] = 0.50 T.
solution:
At $t=0.80\,\text{s}$, the loop is exiting the field, so the changing area rate is $hv$ with $h=0.12\,\text{m}$.
$$\mathcal{E}=Bhv\quad\Rightarrow\quad B=\frac{0.030}{(0.12)(0.50)}=0.50\,\text{T}$$

draft.stem: A rectangular loop moves to the right at $0.50\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ as shown in the figure. At $t=0.80\ \text{s}$, its clockwise induced emf is $+0.030\ \text{V}$. Find the magnitude of the magnetic field.

figure.description: Draw a rectangular conducting loop initially entirely to the left of a uniform-field strip, with its right vertical side just touching the strip's left boundary. The loop is $0.20\ \text{m}$ wide along its direction of motion and $0.12\ \text{m}$ high. Draw the strip extending $0.30\ \text{m}$ horizontally to the right from that boundary, with crosses indicating the magnetic field is into the page; label its magnitude $B$ (unknown). Add a rightward velocity arrow labeled $0.50\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Show a clockwise arrow around the loop to indicate the positive emf direction.

draft.distractor_notes: A: omits the speed factor; B: uses the loop width along the motion instead of its height; D: uses half the loop height as the effective side.
